decisions.decision: Add a project-owned workboard, assignment, criteria, due date, archive and version-checked mutations. Do not transplant the PHP module or introduce a second tenancy model.
Task proof calls the existing REUNIR contribution submit/resubmit/review lifecycle and existing EvidenceReview UI. Recognised state is derived, not a second completion or score record.
Team notes and explicit task/contribution relations stay in project context. General search gets authorised task briefs, not private notes or pending proof text.
Extend existing strict command validation, tenant transaction, optimistic version check, idempotency receipt, outbox, notification and relational persistence mechanisms. No new service or database.

Draft/publish authoring (Alpha 06), structured lesson content (Alpha 08), private lesson resources (Alpha 09) and knowledge checks (Alpha 10) are implemented. Question banks, partial credit, timed checks and file answers stay queued until real community needs justify them: inspect actual files and licences before choosing an approach. Do not transplant whole LMS applications.

Do not copy application files on the strength of the MIT sentence alone. Verify a pinned licence grant, required notices, asset licences and provenance; audit component dependencies and behaviour first.

decisions.decision: Use pinned MIT Tiptap packages for editing; retain the existing command, draft, permission and revision model. Strict JSON validation and a separate React renderer bound content types. Media contacts external hosts only after a learner click.

Extend the existing upload-intent API, Google Cloud Storage adapter and draft/publish/revision model. Bind lesson files to track-scoped upload records by ID, verify the stored file signature, pin the verified object generation, and decide every download through one rule mirroring lesson, space, role and tenant visibility, with restrictive RLS in depth. No donor source copied; the AGPL projects are behavioural references only.

Keep one optional knowledge check inside lesson content so it follows the existing draft, preview, publication and revision model. Score on the server, never send answer keys to learners before the author's reveal rule allows it, refuse answers to a changed check by fingerprint, store each attempt with the quiz it answered as immutable evidence apart from one review by an active owner or administrator who is not the learner, and keep scores out of reputation, completion and credentials. No donor source copied; the AGPL projects are behavioural references only.

Replace decorative track and project art with uploaded covers and a plain neutral panel. Keep every title and detail outside the picture, with only opaque status labels on it. Bind each cover upload to one track or project, resize in the browser to 1,600 pixels (dropping metadata), verify signature and header dimensions on the pinned generation, store a focal point for every crop, and serve bytes through one access rule mirroring the record that displays them, with restrictive RLS in depth. No donor source copied; the AGPL projects are behavioural references only, and axe-core and WCAG were read to understand the checks.

Let explicit, administrator-granted track instructors author and review one track. A grant row names one active member for one track and is never inferred from being shown as the author. One per-track rule decides drafts, history, lesson files, knowledge-check keys, attempts, reviews and the cover, in the domain and in row policies, and suspension ends it at once. Instructors work from a teaching page; Community studio stays for owners, administrators and moderators. No donor source copied; the AGPL projects are behavioural references only.

Offer a community cover library beside uploading: owners and administrators add verified pictures with a short name, and anyone who may change a track or project cover chooses one in the same dialogue, with its own focal point and without copying it. No stock search, access key, remote address or unauthenticated route. Every active member can see library pictures; other communities, visitors and unlisted uploads cannot, in the domain and in row policies. A picture stays while any cover shows it, and removing an unused one deletes its stored file. No donor source copied; the AGPL projects are behavioural references only.

Let a member download their own learning record for one community from their profile, built under their own view (titles, names and answer keys as on screen) yet including every record that is theirs. Give operators an owner-authorised, dry-run-first procedure that erases one member's knowledge-check answers and feedback notices with an audit entry of counts only, through a narrowly scoped delete policy the runtime role cannot use, and one that clears unused cover files before their records. Page long review queues 20 at a time with exact totals, waiting answers oldest first. Account deletion and identity scrubbing stay separate. No donor source copied; the AGPL projects are behavioural references only.

Let a signed-in person delete their own account after re-entering their password and typing a phrase. In one transaction across every community, keep posts, comments, project work, lessons, files, covers and sent messages, attributed to one scrubbed membership shown as Former member; delete their personal records (likes, saved posts, notices, goals, learning record, grants, read state, blocks, private files, invitations to their address and queued mail) and their sign-in. Refuse owners rather than delete or transfer a community. Reword notices that name them unless the name is shared, audit counts only, and let row security admit only the person's own rows while the transaction is marked as their own deletion. No donor source copied; the GPL and AGPL projects are behavioural references only.

Let a community's active owner hand the community to one of its active administrators, after re-entering their password and typing the community's name, with a rate limit. The previous owner stays as an administrator, which only the new owner can change. Only an administrator can receive ownership, so ownership goes only to someone already trusted with running the community. The handover runs under the community lock, writes an audit entry naming both memberships and tells the new owner. A unique index keeps a community to one owner. Owners still cannot delete their account while they own a community; once they have handed each one over, they can. No donor source copied; HumHub is a behavioural reference only.
